berserker.name: Berserker
berserker.blurb: Twelve cards, every one of them overpowered. Win before you run dry: your own empty deck never loses you the game, only your opponent's does.
how: Titan is 16 on every side and Skullsplitter is 15 on one — check which edge is facing you before you trade with either.
Warcamp sends your dying cards back to your hand instead of the graveyard, and charges an opponent two cards to break it.
Undying Axe comes back once a game: to your deck, or straight onto any panel you like.

rock.name: Rock
rock.blurb: Defence soaks up the difference. A Teece with Defence 2 only dies to an attack that beats it by three or more.
how: Colossus is 10 on every side and destroys nothing at all unless your Master Rock Flinger is standing.
Rock Sergeant pays every other ally its own Defence, and Stoneheart pays its wearer +1 for each point it has — the deck stacks Defence, then spends it as attack.
Muckraider and Bedrock cannot lose attributes at all, and cannot be selected by enemy effects.

ogre.name: Ogre
ogre.blurb: Shove everything. Ogres move enemies around and the penalties they hand out are permanent, so a shoved Teece never recovers. Negative attributes are lethal.
how: Almost every Ogre moves something as it lands, and the -2 it hands out sticks for the rest of the game.
Ogre Trapper punishes movement however it happened, so your own shoves feed it too.
Sinkhole destroys whatever moves onto it. Springshelf pays +5 to whatever moves on — and nothing to a Teece played straight there.

robot.name: Robot
robot.blurb: Every Robot Flies, and Drones roll off the line all game. Drones are 3/3/3/3 Tokens that also Fly — they block, they kill, and several Robots pay you for keeping them moving.
how: Drones are 3/3/3/3 flying Tokens, and Tokens never count toward winning: they are board, not lead.
Swarm Node, Hangar Guard and Drone Tether all pay the Drones; Overclocker and Signal Relay pay for movement instead.
War Machine is 11 on every side and brings three more Drones down with it.

gadget.name: Gadget
gadget.blurb: Almost every card asks you to choose a mode. The deck is built to cheat that choice — fire every mode at once, fire the chosen one twice, or switch modes off for both players entirely.
how: Null Module, Preset, Coupling Rig and Grand Apparatus all bend the next choice: every mode at once, or the chosen mode twice.
Safety Interlock switches your OWN modalities off — while it stands, your cards that offer a choice simply do nothing.
Modular Platform sells the same trick as ground, and the size you give it decides which trick you get.

time.name: Time
time.blurb: Cards that grow or rot on a clock. Every Teece ages at the start of your turn; some come of age into something far bigger, others decay every turn you keep them.
how: Acorn and Long Game are nearly worthless for two turns and then 10 and 12 on every side.
Fast Forward, Timekeeper, Whetted Blade and Last Breath all push clocks forward — that is how you collect early.
Chronoplate stops a clock dead, which is what saves a Fading Titan. Sundial doubles it, which is only ever good on something growing.

witch.name: Witch
witch.blurb: Eight Curses instead of equipment or ground. Witches are physically fragile, but a Curse can silence a player, freeze their Teece in hand, turn one against them, or raze a panel off the board for good.
how: Curse of Freezing is the trump: they cannot play a Teece at all, and you cannot win the game until it lifts — it buys time, not the win.
Most Witches trigger on you playing magic at all, so a cheap Curse is also a growth spurt.
Coven Matriarch turns every Curse of yours that picks one player into one that hits everybody — you included.

bomb.name: Bomb
bomb.blurb: Crazy area-of-effect damage that risks blowing itself up too. Lay Mines to control the board, then turn the damage into a boost with Blast Ward.
how: Blast Ward inverts the whole deck: the Teece wearing it gains whatever it would have lost.
Mines sit on empty panels for -2 as anything arrives, and Chain Charge, Minefield and Overcharged Warhead all make them bigger.
Unstable Warhead destroys itself the moment anything targets it or takes a single point off it.

nature.name: Nature
nature.blurb: Plants that feed each other. Almost every card hands out a permanent bonus, and the bonuses stack all game — but every plant is soft at the bottom, so watch the edge it is standing on.
how: Nearly every plant is thin on its bottom edge — Sapling 1, Elder Willow 1, Mother Tree 1 — so the panel above it is where it dies.
Hothouse Orchid and Sunlit Loam double every positive effect, and the bonuses here are permanent, so they compound all game.
Plant Pot is +20 on the bottom side alone, which is exactly the edge the deck keeps leaving open.

pixie.name: Pixie
pixie.blurb: Tiny flying creatures with almost no numbers and an enormous amount of magic. Every pixie flies, and the deck keeps pulling magic back out of graveyards, decks and thin air — then bends what is on the field with it: minds taken, Teece stretched or shrunk, wings bought by the turn.
how: Pixies are 0s, 1s and 2s. They are not meant to fight — they are meant to keep casting.
Trickspinner, Wisp of Nothing and Enchantment conjure magic out of nothing; Thieving Sprite, Grave Pixie and Echo Pixie pull it back out of graveyards and decks.
Pixie Queen gives every other pixie of yours +10, and is the one card that turns the swarm into a board.

spider.name: Spider
spider.blurb: A cannibal swarm. The Web is on the field from the first turn, covering every panel but the corners. Every Spider Teece and Spiderling standing on it can Skitter one space each turn, and a Spiderling has +1 Defence there. Spiders pour out 4/4/4/4 Spiderlings and then eat them to pay for everything else.
how: Spiderlings are Tokens, and Tokens never count toward winning: they are fuel and board, never a lead.
The corners are never Web, which makes them the one place a Spiderling gets neither Skitter nor its extra Defence.
Brood Mother reprints every Spiderling on the Web at 12/12/12/12 — either side's — and stops them being sacrificed at all.

vampire.name: Vampire
vampire.blurb: They grow by taking. Drain X pulls X off a Teece and hands the drinker exactly what it managed to take — which is not always X, because Steadfast gives up nothing and the deck's own castle, catalyst and fangs all bend the number on the way.
how: Parasite has to bite twice on each of your turns, from your own side, or it withers and dies.
Enhanced Fangs doubles what you take. Vampire Castle and Transfusion Catalyst double everything either way, up and down alike.
Blood Bank stores every drain anything else makes, and spends the lot as one bite once a turn.

zombie.name: Zombie
zombie.blurb: They come back when you kill them. X Undying Y means X returns a game, each worth Y more than the last, on any free panel you choose. A returned Teece has no protection, so placement is what keeps it alive. The rest of the deck works both graveyards: summoning out of them, stealing from the enemy's, and taking cards back to hand.
how: The return count belongs to the card, not the body, so bouncing a zombie back to hand does not launder it. Back Again and Death's Avatar are the two that wind it back.
Silence stops it getting up. A silenced zombie stays down.
Plague Winds hands every ally +1 and every enemy -1 at the end of every turn — both sides' turns, not just yours.

tictactoe.name: Tic Tac Toe
tictactoe.blurb: A second board laid over the first. Every Teece here is an X, an O, or both, and the two Toerrains mark a bare panel on their own. Three of one letter in a straight line takes the game at the end of that turn, however far behind you are on bodies.
how: A body covers the ground it stands on, so standing on their Toerrain blocks that line instead of joining it.
The board lights up any line standing at two with its last panel still open, whoever holds it.
bOX and XOD count as an X and an O at once, which is two lines from one body.

solar.name: Solar
solar.blurb: The sun at the corner of the board turns to a moon at the start of every round, so each of your own turns runs the other way from the last. Half of what this deck prints is worth having in one half of the cycle and worth nothing in the other — so play the sky, not just the card.
how: A card that only works in one half of the cycle tells you so when you play it in the other.
Equips read the sky too: Twilight Cloak is +3 Defence by night, and +7 with Flying by day.
Stopped Sundial pins the sky where it stands — the round stops turning it, and no card can turn it either.

army.name: Army
army.blurb: A deck that is paid for its shape. Almost nothing here is worth much standing alone — Teece gain attributes, Ranged, March and cover for standing beside an ally, and the equips pay for lines, triangles and a lone point. Field Marshal Marshall ends the geometry altogether: while he stands, every Teece on the field counts as adjacent to all of its allies, wherever they are.
how: Beside means the four panels a side touches, never a diagonal. Line Formation is the only card here that counts diagonals, and it counts them as lines rather than as neighbours.
Brigadeer Ryan and Brigadeer Bryan call each other up: play one and the other may go down the same turn without spending your Teece play. Side by side they are +10 each.
Scout Stout is paid for having its back to the board — two sides on a corner, one side and Ranged on an edge, all four in the middle — so it wants the panel nobody else does.

garbage.name: Garbage
garbage.blurb: Twice the deck and twice the turn: forty-odd cards, two Teece plays and two draws every turn. Nothing here is worth much on its own, and most of it pays for itself by being thrown away — the graveyard is the stockpile, and Living Dump, Trash King and the Dumpster all read the size of the heap behind you.
how: Two Teece a turn and two cards a turn are the deck's own rule, not a card's: they hold for as long as you are playing Garbage. Garbage Soul adds a third of each while it stands.
The graveyard is a resource. Living Dump grows with it, Trash King eats it for attributes, Garbage Man and Racoon fish cards back out of it, and Banana Peel and the Dumpster spend it.
Fire sits on a panel rather than on a Teece. Anything standing in one has -4 while it burns, and it burns until the start of the turn of whoever lit it.

apocalypse.name: Apocalypse
apocalypse.blurb: The end arrives on schedule. The four Horsemen are lifted back out of the shuffle and stacked on top of your deck, so they are your opening hand, and each one played drags a second out of it silenced. Everything after them is paid for in cards: the graveyard is this deck's second resource, and two of its three ways to clear the field are bought with discards.

madness.name: Madness
madness.blurb: Played out of the graveyard rather than into it. Almost every card does its work on the way OUT of your hand, and four of them let you throw themselves away whenever you like, so a discard is a move rather than a loss. Two cards catch discards before they land: a Pocket Dimension that hands them all back at the end of the turn, and a Library that shelves them as a wall.

formats.name: Free-for-all
formats.blurb: Three separate sides. Everyone is your enemy, and the first side four Teece ahead of the next best wins.

formats.name: You and one computer
formats.blurb: You and the first computer fight as one side against the second. Allies never damage each other and win together.

formats.name: You against both
formats.blurb: Both computers are allied against you. Hardest of the three, and the reason the difficulty rating goes below zero.
